questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A mix of many things

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go on exchange for a full academic year, which left me with few options, among them University of California, Berkeley. After having looked at my options I decided to choose Berkeley for my reasons:
- Highly rated academic school
- I have family nearby
- Interesting history
- I've never been to the US

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Go for two semesters, not one and apply for housing at the BSC system the moment you consider going to Berkeley.

I really loved my stay and I would recommend anyone to go, and if possible in any way I would encourage people to go for a full year rather than only spending one semester abroad. The second semester was by far the best, because I already had established a connections with people, settled in the area  and I received new, unforeseen opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I must admit I don't remember, so I guess everything was OK

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is a mandatory, expensive Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) which is a huge event for all new students. It is kind of a mess logistically and I've heard some people manage to waive the attendance. I met some people during GBO but did not stay in contact with any of them during the school year.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: People are extremely helpful but the first days have way too many events. I would recommend going to everyting, but also taking your own time walking aimlessly around campus and entering random buildings on your own to get your own perspective of the university. That is how I found the Student Musical Activities Center

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I lived with familiy the first two weeks because I didn't get housing offer before that.
Apply for the BSC now even if you are only slightly considering Berkeley.
https://www.bsc.coop/
It is much cheaper and more fun than any other alternative. As a comparision:
2 semesters of housing at Coop INCLUDING food: $8700
4 months of housing at I-House: >$8800
Note:
I lived at Casa Zimbabwe (CZ or die). It is pretty messy, but you meet people from many different areas. One of my best friends from this place had fled his own country to become a journalist in the US.
If you decide to live in a coop, you should expect to be challenged on values and ability to accept other cultures and mindsets. People do many different drugs, but they have a much healthier attitude toward  recreational drug use than Danes have to alcohol.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Coops.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Apply for coops today - that will save you money per month than most student grants will give you!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It is relatively competitve to get the calsses you want, but it's all about playing the long game. Many people drop classes during the first two weeks and I have rarely met people who waited until the end of the deadline and still hadn't got what they wanted/needed. 
In the summer you have to choose classes and during the first 2-4 weeks you can drop classes. That is very helpful in making decisions about what is the  most interesting. I actuall ylike thiss system better than the KU system, because there is way more flexibility.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know of any

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted. I took a Chinese class which had different recommendations than the rest, but I ended up talking to the instructor directly and then they allowed me to join the class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find classes you want, go to the lectures in the beginning and just keep your place on the wait list and you will get in (except for really tiny music production classes).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took 100- level classes in statistics and they where much more applied than the equvalent are at Copenhagen University, but they ave way more exercises. I think the general consesus among exchange students is that there is way more evaluation during the semester and that you almost don't need to study for the exam because the final is only 30%. People say they are super busy at all times. I had a course load of 15 units the first semester and 13 units the second semester, and I still had plenty of time to play music, go for runs and enjoy the weekends. Be prepared to do many assignments and get used to just doing them, then you can keep your evenings of.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more tests and midterms, more concrete tasks. The exercises are less useful, since the TA useful just shows the solutions rather than letting yourself figure stuff out.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
STAT 135 Concepts of statistics (4 units) - brilliant, but tough, class. A bit like MStat and StatMet. I had 10 assignments, 4 quizzes, 1 midterm and 1 final
STAT 133 Concepts of computing with data (3 units) - Very easy, great for getting to know R, would maybe not prioritize again
PHILOS 128 Philosphy of Science (4 units) - A substitute for Videnskabsteori. It was very different from VT, but was very interesting and it is actually pretty great to be challenged in a different way of writing and thinking
ENE RES 160 CLIMATE JUSTICE  (4 units)- super important class! It is mostly a general introduction the the term Justice and the consequences of climate changes.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
CHINESE 100B Advanced Chinese - the most time consuming class I took. Taking a language class is amazing and impossible to do at Copenhagen!
STAT 151A Linear Modelling: Applications and Theory: The instructor was new and the structue not too great. Would not recommend
CS 61A (programming class) -The most wellstructured class I've ever taken! Great exercises e.t.c., take the class if you're intereseted in learning to program and don't worry about the hype about the difficulty. There is plenty of help available if necessary and it is a bit like solving sudokus

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend people to do classes that are not possible at KU! Remeber that you are here to learn something different that people back home, spend time taking classes in humanities

ENE RES 160 CLIMATE JUSTICE 
CS61A

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Car insurance and parking was very expensive. Food is way more expensive than in Denmark! In addition the school has many extra fees I had never heard of (approx 3500 DKK) at the beginning of the semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many things, especially consulting and dance clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of the SMA (Student music activities) and played in the UC Bigband and World Music Ensemble (WME). WME was great if you want a more spiritual discussion of music.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for runs in the hill! The stonewall panorama trial is amazing, Yosemite overrated. Go to all the cool performances, lectures and conferences on campus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. People don't drink as much alchol which is actually pretty nice. On the other hand you will hear al ot about other substances. I think it's very important to get a more nuanced look and Danish alcohol culture! In addition most students and Berkeley are 18-22, so you may feel slightly old at times

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in a coop. People a young but amazing

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing. It was amazing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural diverisity and access to other types of music and philosphies. Remember to get non-exchange friends and get to know "local" life in the US. Europe will also be there when you come back from exchange.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Apply for living at a coop this moment
coop.bsc
(seriously). You can end up spending way more time and eneryg living at a shittier place if you don't-
- Accept people are different, acknowledge the privileges most Danes grow up with and enjoy the diversity
- Don't worry too much about school. Do you homework and remember the teacher wants you to succeed and are very helpful at office hours!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't forget that this is a once in a life time opportunity and immerse yourself in the culture. Don't spend too much time alone watching movies, but remember to take care of yourself when needed. Most people around you are in the same boat (moving far away from home to a new school), join a club and prioritize people over school work!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing so much diversity

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that it would be over

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
